title: Late Bronze Age collapse in the eastern Mediterranean
summary: Between about 1250 and 1150 BCE, many cities and states of the eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia were destroyed or declined, including Ugarit, Hattusa and Pylos, and the Hittite and Mycenaean systems ended. Sources list earthquakes, drought, invasions by Sea Peoples and trade disruption, and stress that no single cause explains it.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the start as c. 1250 or c. 1225 BCE (World History Encyclopedia notes estimates range from 1250 to 1177 BCE). Decline continued unevenly afterwards.

where.modern_name: Ugarit (Ras Shamra), Syria, used as a marker only; the collapse spans the eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia
where.historical_name: Eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia, Late Bronze Age; Ugarit lay in the Levant

importance.justification: A region-wide breakdown of the Late Bronze Age palace states and trade networks that preceded the Greek and Near Eastern dark ages.

reviewer_note: The pin is Ugarit as a marker for a region-wide process, hence the 1200 km uncertainty; it is not a single event site. Start date varies by source (c. 1250 vs 1225 BCE). Cause is not settled and the summary lists only factors named on the opened pages.
